_about: How to verify and fix each preflight check, like the SE demo kit's preflight help. Keyed by check ID; an ID ending in -* matches a prefix (zia-read-* covers every ZIA area). Shown under each check as 'How to verify'.

keychain.what: The kit writes, reads and deletes a test value in this computer's keychain.
keychain.why: API client secrets, the provisioning key and test users' passwords live only in the keychain, never in files.
verify: Mac: Keychain Access opens and the login keychain is unlocked.
Windows: Credential Manager opens.
fix: Mac: unlock the login keychain (Keychain Access > File > Unlock).
Linux: install and start a keyring service (gnome-keyring or KWallet).

connect.what: The POV's API client signs in to the tenant.
connect.why: Nothing else can be checked or built without it.
verify: Administration > API > OneAPI > API Clients lists the client, and its client ID matches the one in Connect.
fix: Check the vanity domain, client ID and secret in Connect.
A lost secret: create a new one on the client and enter it in Connect.

zia-read-*.what: The kit lists one ZIA area (rules, categories, groups...) with the API client.
zia-read-*.why: The kit reads each area before planning, to find the customer's own objects and keep clear of them.
verify: Open the POV's API client: Internet Access (ZIA) is listed with at least view access.
fix: Give the client view access to this ZIA area (the role spec lists them all).

zia-activation.what: The kit reads ZIA's activation status.
zia-activation.why: ZIA changes take effect only when activated, and activation applies everyone's pending changes. The kit never activates someone else's work.
verify: The console's Activation menu shows no pending changes.
fix: Ask the admin to activate or discard their pending changes.

zia-names.what: The kit looks for objects in the tenant with the names the POV would use, that aren't this POV's.
zia-names.why: The kit never takes over or overwrites an object it didn't make.
verify: The detail lists each taken name and whether another POV on this laptop owns it.
fix: Give this POV its own prefix (Use prefix ZPOV2 on the Apply step, or `pov-kit set prefix ZPOV2`), then approve the new change list.
Or remove the other POV first (Handover).

zia-pilot.what: The kit looks for the pilot group the POV's rules will apply to.
zia-pilot.why: Every POV rule applies to the pilot group only, so nobody else in the company is affected.
verify: Pilot users shows the group, or the POV makes its own.
fix: Choose who tests in the Pilot users step.

zid-read.what: The kit lists ZIdentity users and groups.
zid-read.why: The POV can make its own pilot group and test users in ZIdentity, and checks pilot users' entitlements there.
verify: The POV's API client lists ZIdentity with view access (and user management, if the POV makes its group).
fix: Give the client ZIdentity access from the role spec, or name an existing pilot group instead (Pilot users step).

id-entitlements.what: For each pilot user, the kit reads ZIdentity's service entitlements.
id-entitlements.why: Unentitled users aren't sent to ZIA, so the POV's rules never see their traffic.
verify: The entitlements page (search: Entitlement) lists the pilot group under Internet & SaaS.
fix: Entitle the pilot group to Internet & SaaS (a step for the customer's admin).

id-read.what: The kit reads who the pilot users are, across products.
id-read.why: It needs them to scope every rule and check the users exist.
verify: The detail says what couldn't be read.
fix: Give the API client view access to ZIdentity and ZIA users (role spec).

id-zia-group.what: The kit checks each named pilot user is a member of the pilot group.
id-zia-group.why: The POV's rules apply only to members, so a user outside the group isn't part of the POV.
verify: The customer's directory lists each pilot user in the group.
fix: Add them to the group in the customer's directory (it syncs to Zscaler).
id-zia-group.retest: Run checks again (after the directory syncs).

zpa-customer-id.what: The kit looks for the ZPA customer ID saved in Connect.
zpa-customer-id.why: ZPA's API needs it, even through OneAPI.
verify: Administration > API > Legacy API > Private Access API > Copy ID shows it.
fix: Paste it into Connect > ZPA customer ID.

zpa-read.what: The kit reads ZPA with the customer ID.
zpa-read.why: Planning ZPA needs the tenant's segments, groups and certificates.
verify: The customer ID in Connect matches Copy ID digit for digit, and the client has view access to ZPA.
fix: Copy the customer ID again (a 404 means it's wrong or cut short).
Add ZPA access to the API client.

zpa-cert.what: The kit looks for ZPA's connector enrollment certificate.
zpa-cert.why: The POV's provisioning key needs it to enroll App Connectors.
verify: Every ZPA tenant has one named Connector (search: Enrollment Certificates).
fix: Check the API client's view access to ZPA certificates.

zpa-overlap.what: The kit checks the POV app's domains aren't already in one of the customer's segments.
zpa-overlap.why: ZPA matches the most specific segment, so a shared domain would follow the customer's rules, not the POV's.
verify: The detail names the customer's segment that has the domain.
fix: Use the kit's test app, or a domain only the POV uses (Pilot users / ZPA settings).

zpa-pilot.what: The kit looks for the pilot users in ZPA (a SCIM group, or a SAML attribute).
zpa-pilot.why: ZPA takes users from the identity provider, so the access rule needs a ZPA-side way to match them.
verify: ZPA lists the group under the IdP's SCIM groups, or the SAML attribute under its SAML attributes.
fix: Set the SCIM group or SAML attribute in Pilot users (ZPA).

zcc-read.what: The kit reads Client Connector's app and forwarding profiles.
zcc-read.why: The POV copies the default Windows profiles for its own pilot-only profile.
verify: The API client lists Client Connector with view access.
fix: Add Client Connector access from the role spec.

zcc-source.what: The kit looks for a default Windows app profile with a forwarding profile to copy.
zcc-source.why: Without one, the POV's profiles are built by hand (a step for people after Apply).
verify: Search the console menu for App Profiles: a default Windows profile exists.
fix: Nothing to fix: follow the 'Build the POV's Client Connector profiles by hand' step after Apply.

aiguard-read.what: The kit reads AI Guard's apps, policies and rules.
aiguard-read.why: The POV adds its own app and policy next to the customer's, never changing theirs.
verify: The API client lists ZGUARD (AI Guard) with view access.
fix: Add AI Guard access from the role spec.

casb-read.why: The POV's CASB DLP rule scans a connected SaaS tenant.
verify: The API client lists ZIA SaaS security with view access.
fix: Add the access from the role spec.

casb-tenant.what: The kit looks for a connected SaaS tenant.
casb-tenant.why: The CASB criterion needs one to scan.
verify: Search: SaaS Application Tenants. One shows as connected.
fix: Connect one (the step for people, with the SaaS admin's consent).

zdx-*.what: The kit reads ZDX with the POV's API client.
zdx-*.why: ZDX criteria need the pilot devices' scores and probes.
verify: The API client has a ZDX role.
fix: Give the client a view-only ZDX role (a step for people).
